name: Ancient Empires (Mauryan & Gupta)
description: Period of imperial rule under the Mauryans (Emperor Ashoka) and Guptas, during which Mahasthangarh (Pundranagara) and Tamralipta (Tamluk) flourished as major urban trade hubs.

name: Pala Empire
description: Mahayana Buddhist imperial dynasty founded by Gopala that unified Bengal and Bihar, founding famous monastic universities at Nalanda, Vikramashila, and Somapura Mahavihara.

name: Sena Dynasty
description: Hindu dynasty originating from South India that succeeded the Palas in Bengal proper. Patronized Sanskrit literature (Jayadeva's Gita Govinda).

name: Delhi Sultanate & Early Governors
description: Began with Muhammad Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquest of Lakhnauti in 1204. Characterized by frequent rebellions by Bengal governors against the Delhi Sultanate.

name: Bengal Sultanate
description: Golden age of independent Islamic monarchy founded by Shamsuddin Iliyas Shah. Famous for magnificent brick mosque architecture (Adina Mosque, Sona Masjid), Bengali literature patrons, and international maritime trade.

name: Mughal Subah Bangalah
description: Incorporated into Akbar's Mughal Empire after the defeat of Daud Khan Karrani at Rajmahal (1576). Subahdar Islam Khan I moved the capital to Dacca in 1610. Known as the 'Paradise of Nations'.

name: Nawabs of Bengal
description: De facto independent principality established by Murshid Quli Khan, who moved the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad. Ended with Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah's betrayal at Plassey in 1757.

name: East India Company Rule
description: Colonial mercantile rule following the Battles of Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764). Diwani rights acquired in 1765, leading to the Permanent Settlement of 1793 and Calcutta's rise as imperial center.

name: British Raj (Crown Rule)
description: Direct administration under the British Crown following the 1857 Revolt. The Lieutenant-Governorship of Bengal governed the province until the 1905 Partition and 1911 reorganisation.
